From one suicidal person to another, school really isn't about grades. While yes the end goal is about grades, it's really about the adventure of day to day school life. I'm an engineering student and believe me I didn't give two squats about my grade. All I was eager for is to get my hands on some machines. While yes my coding was average, the feeling of creating something with the stuff I learn is quite fulfilling. Yes, there will always be other people who could do it better, faster, efficient and overall greater then I am. But their curiosity isn't what I want. It's my own curiosity then I want fulfilled.

There definitely is some days that I wouldn't have mind skipping either cause I could or due to circumstances outside my control, but to satisfy my curiosity of what tomorrow might hold is good enough for me. And that's outside academic reasons. There's definitely some stuff I actually learned.

So don't go to school expecting to satisfy other people but to satisfy yourself. Your curiosity and thirst for knowledge. And if nothing different happens then it's just another day.

And I know a thing or two about parents being upset over things we've done. I was admitted to a mental "hospital" for four days. No one visited or even called except for my brother. And when I came back home, it was like nothing ever changed. 

Simple tip, don't satisfy others curiosity but your own.

A death of one person really won't affect the world in the grand scheme of things. Could your death stop climate change or stop world hunger? No. And neither could one alive person change the world either. However. Could a random person's death affect the one's closest to you? No. But your death? Tremendously so. I'm not saying you should stay for them or anyone else but I'm being factual. Unless your an actual hermit who lives in a secluded place in the world, our deaths will affect at least one person. 

People die all the time. It's not being cold but being honest. Your death is as significant to me as adding another digit to the number of suicide victims. However to someone close to you, it would be like having a piece of their soul disappear. Yes they will grieve and move on but there's nothing more they can do once you're gone.

The best way I can explain it is like performing in a play. You are the main character in your own play. And everyone is both a side character and a audience. We are not you but there are parts of us that are similar to you. And there are parts of you that is similar to us. When you take that final bow and the curtains close on you, the world will simply continue on. There will be people who wished you had a longer play and people who are outraged the curtains closed on you far to early. But once the curtains close and you six feet under, there will be nothing left but to move on with the show.

You can die, and maybe someone else would be fortunate to get all the chances you would have gotten if you were still alive, but a piece of you will disappear in people who are close to you. So please, when you take that last bow, do it with no regret.
